name: The Cold War, nuclear threat and the bomb
description: Superpower rivalry, McCarthyism, nuclear deterrence and the fear of annihilation as subjects and pressures, from Nineteen Eighty-Four to Gravity's Rainbow.

name: Decolonisation, the end of empire and the new nation
description: Independence, the legacy of colonial rule and the making of postcolonial nations and their disillusionments.

name: Migration, exile and diaspora
description: Movement between countries and cultures: arrival, displacement, return, divided belonging and the second generation.

name: Race, racism and the struggle for civil rights
description: Racial oppression and resistance, segregation and apartheid, Black identity and the civil-rights and Black Power movements.

name: Gender, feminism and women's lives
description: The social construction of womanhood and manhood, women's work, bodies and voices, and feminist challenges to patriarchy.

name: Sexuality, desire and the closet
description: Sexual identity and desire, secrecy and coming out, homophobia, sexual liberation and its limits.

name: Class, labour and social mobility
description: Work, poverty, class consciousness and the scholarship child or the climber moving between classes.

name: War, combat and its aftermath
description: The Second World War, Korea, Vietnam and colonial wars experienced at the front and remembered afterwards.

name: The Holocaust, atrocity and historical memory
description: Genocide, survival and the obligation to remember, and the problem of representing atrocity.

name: Identity, authenticity and the divided self
description: The search for an authentic self amid social roles, doubles, masks and multiple identities.

name: Alienation, absurdity and existential freedom
description: Meaninglessness, estrangement and the burden of choice in a world without given values.

name: Family, marriage and domestic life
description: Parents and children, marriages made and broken, the home as refuge and trap.

name: Childhood, adolescence and coming of age
description: Growing up, initiation, lost innocence and the formation of the young self.

name: Faith, doubt and the sacred
description: Religious belief and unbelief, grace and sin, and spiritual searching in a secularising world.

name: Madness, breakdown and confinement
description: Mental illness, psychiatric institutions, breakdown and the boundary between sanity and insight.

name: Language, writing and the limits of representation
description: Literature's awareness of its own medium: naming, silence, translation and what words cannot reach.

name: History, truth and the uses of the past
description: How the past is recorded, invented, contested and made to serve the present.

name: Technology, media and consumer society
description: Television, advertising, computers and the mass market as forces reshaping perception and desire.

name: The city, the suburb and modern space
description: Urban and suburban environments, their anonymity, energy, segregation and decay.

name: Land, place and regional belonging
description: Attachment to a particular landscape or region, rural life and its disappearance.

name: Nature, ecology and environmental crisis
description: The natural world as value and as endangered, from Silent Spring to the climate.

name: Power, the state and surveillance
description: Political authority, totalitarianism, bureaucracy, policing and the individual's freedom.

name: Violence, crime and justice
description: Crime and punishment, the law and its failures, and violence private and public.

name: Death, illness and mourning
description: Mortality, grief, disease (including the AIDS epidemic) and the rituals of loss.

name: Art, the artist and the creative life
description: The making of art, the artist's vocation and conflicts between art and life.

name: Indigenous survival, land and sovereignty
description: Indigenous peoples' dispossession, cultural survival, ceremony and claims to land and self-government.

name: Nationhood and national identity
description: What it means to be Scottish, Welsh, Irish, Canadian, Australian, Indian, Nigerian or American, and who decides.

name: Myth, folklore and the supernatural
description: Ancient story, folk belief and the uncanny reworked in modern writing.

name: Love, intimacy and loss
description: Romantic and erotic love, friendship and their ending.

name: Education, institutions and the academy
description: Schools and universities, their rituals and hierarchies, and learning as liberation or constraint.

name: Counterculture, drugs and rebellion
description: The youth revolt, drugs, music and alternative ways of living in the 1950s–70s.

name: Utopia, dystopia and imagined futures
description: Visions of ideal or nightmarish societies and of the human future.

name: Memory, trauma and testimony
description: How individuals and communities remember suffering, bear witness and seek recovery.
